newsitem.title: USA: FASB may back off "poolings" threat - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FASB may back off "poolings" threat - WSJ.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board may not follow through with its threat to restrict or abolish "poolings of interest", a method used by companies in accounting for large stock mergers, the Wall Street Journal said on Tuesday.
The Journal reported in its electronic edition that an FASB official said the board may keep the poolings but make purchase accounting less onerous by eliminating amortisation of goodwill.
Poolings let companies involved in a merger add together the book value of their assets and liabilities to avoid big hits against future earnings of the combined entity.

Under the purchase-accounting method, the acquiring company records the price of the acquisition, rather than the pooling of the two companies' assets. The buyer must then gradually write off goodwill against earnings for as long as 40 years.
Goodwill is considered the premium paid beyond the fair-market value of the acquired company's assets.
The FASB said it plans to begin discussing the issue this fall.
